samples.summary: `paste` normalizes the *origin of the whole pasted grid* to a merge anchor, so a multi-cell paste onto a row/column selection whose head cell is merge-covered lands one or more rows/columns off and overwrites unrelated cells
samples.evidence: `const destStart = this.normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell);` (sheet.ts:2241) feeds `string2grid(destStart, text)` (2294), `html2grid(destStart, ...)` (2290) and `relocateGrid(..., destStart)` (2248). `selectRow(row)` sets `activeCell = { r: row, c: 1 }` (sheet.ts:3443) without normalizing. With a vertical merge A2:A4 and `selectRow(3)`, destStart becomes A2, so pasting a full row `x\ty\tz` writes A2/B2/C2 instead of A3/B3/C3 — it silently overwrites row 2's B and C (which are not merged at all) and leaves row 3 untouched. Same for `selectColumn(col)` (sheet.ts:3456) with a horizontal merge in row 1: the whole paste shifts a column left. The new behaviour is only needed for the single-cell/anchor case the diff's own comment describes; shifting the grid origin for a multi-cell paste is a destination error, not an anchor normalization. The added tests only cover single-column/single-value cases (merge.test.ts `should paste an external grid from the anchor too`), so the wrong-row multi-column case is untested.

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` still uses the pasted grid's bounding box, so a paste that re-creates merged blocks selects a region smaller than what was pasted (a single merged block collapses to a one-cell selection)
samples.evidence: `const [from, to] = rangeOf(grid)` (sheet.ts:2615). `planPasteMerges` explicitly documents that a merged block's covered cells are absent from the grid so its bounding box is smaller than the block (sheet.ts:2390-2393), yet the selection is still computed from that box. Copying merged block A1:B1 and pasting at A3 yields grid `{A3}`, so `selectPastedRange` takes the `from.r===to.r && from.c===to.c` branch and just moves the active cell rather than selecting A3:B3. Wrong post-paste selection state, no data loss.

samples.summary: The copy buffer now survives every paste but is still never invalidated by structural edits, widening the window in which a repeat internal paste relocates formulas/merges by a stale delta
samples.evidence: `copyBuffer` is only assigned in `copy`/`cut`, cleared in `clearCopyBuffer` and on a consumed cut (`sheet.ts:2141,2155,2176,2286`); nothing in `insertRows`/`deleteRows`/`insertColumns` touches it (grep for `copyBuffer` in sheet.ts returns only those lines). Both view paste paths stopped calling `clearCopyBuffer()` (view/worksheet.ts:4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:728), so after a copy the buffer persists indefinitely; if rows/columns are inserted or deleted between pastes, `deltaRow/deltaCol` are computed from a `sourceRange` that no longer matches the live grid (sheet.ts:2250-2251) and both the relocated formulas and the re-created merge anchors are offset wrongly. Largely pre-existing for the first paste, newly reachable for subsequent ones.

samples.summary: The new freeze-boundary invariant (`merge-paste-frozen` / `merge-move-frozen`) is bypassable: `setFreezePane` sets `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` with no check against existing merged blocks
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2429-2433) and `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2685-2695) refuse operations that would land a block across a freeze boundary, citing an invariant the renderer assumes. But `setFreezePane(frozenRows, frozenCols)` (sheet.ts:514-518) simply assigns both fields and persists them, so freezing rows 1-2 while a block spans rows 2-3 reaches exactly the state the new refusals exist to prevent. `loadFreezePane` (sheet.ts:523) likewise restores whatever the store holds. The guard therefore does not establish the invariant it claims.

samples.summary: `rangeOf` still returns `[{Infinity,Infinity},{-Infinity,-Infinity}]` for an empty grid, and the new exported/tested API has no guard for that
samples.evidence: The loop initialises `minR = Infinity … maxC = -Infinity` and returns them unchanged when `grid.keys()` is empty (coordinates.ts:23-40). Behaviour matches the old `Math.min(...[])`, and the only caller guards with `if (grid.size === 0) return` (sheet.ts:2613), so nothing breaks today — but the function is now exported and covered by tests, so a future caller gets nonsensical bounds instead of an error.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present as described and the bad path is reachable. paste() computes one origin `destStart = this.normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell)` (sheet.ts:2241) and uses it as the top-left of the ENTIRE pasted block: string2grid(destStart, text) (2294), html2grid(html, destStart) (2290), relocateGrid(..., destStart) (2245-2251). normalizeRefToAnchor (844-846 via getAnchorSrefForRef 835-839) maps a merge-covered ref to the anchor, and string2grid (grids.ts:113-126) offsets every cell from that ref, so with merge A2:A4 and selectRow(3) (which sets activeCell={r:3,c:1} without normalizing, sheet.ts:3441-3449) a paste of `x\ty\tz` writes A2/B2/C2 — B2 and C2 are outside the column-A merge and are silently overwritten, while row 3 is never written. setGrid (memory.ts:260-266, yorkie-store.ts:385-415) writes each sref verbatim, so nothing downstream re-anchors or clips the shift. The external TSV/HTML branch builds no merge plan, so the plan.ok refusal (2270-2273) cannot catch it. Reachable in normal use: row-header click -> selectRow (view/worksheet.ts:3805) then Ctrl+V -> sheet.paste (view/worksheet.ts:4947, spreadsheet.ts:728) with no selectionType or grid-size guard. Same shape for selectColumn (3454-3462) with a horizontal merge in row 1. Added tests (merge.test.ts:747-791) only cover single-value pastes, so the multi-cell case is untested. In-lane (wrong destination / data overwrite), and impact is data loss on a real path.
